title: Add workload-aware batch templates and quantization safety-net
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce workload-aware batch templates and a runtime safety-net for quantization profiles. Reduces per-token cost by 8-15% across a mix of chat and single-turn workloads; adds opt-in telemetry and guardrails to prevent quality regressions.
commits: a1f7c3d: add workload template schema and validator
b2e9d44: implement template selector in batching router
c3d2f88: add quantization safety-net and fallback rules
d4f6b90: unit tests + integration smoke harness
e5a0c11: docs and examples for template authoring
description:
Motivation: We saw recurring manual tweaks to batching and quant profiles for different workload shapes (short chat bursts vs long single-turn summaries). Teams waste cycles trying to find safe quant+batch combos that don't regress quality. This PR introduces two orthogonal pieces: 1) workload-aware batch templates: curated, parameterized batch/caching templates keyed by workload fingerprint (seq-dist, request-rate, kv-cache-hit-rate) so users can pick or auto-apply sensible defaults; 2) quantization safety-net: a runtime guard that validates quantized model outputs against a lightweight quality proxy and falls back to a compatible (higher-precision) variant when thresholds are crossed.

What this changes (summary): - New template schema + validator (YAML) and an authoring guide. - Template selector in the batching router that scores candidate templates against live workload fingerprints and applies the highest scoring template within SLO constraints. - Safety-net path that runs a fast proxy eval on sampled outputs; if degradation detected, requests route to a fallback model variant automatically for the batch. - Telemetry events and console summaries for template recommendations and safety-net triggers. - Integration tests and benchmarking harness additions used for evaluation.

Checklist: - [x] API and runtime changes implemented. - [x] Unit tests for the selector and safety-net logic. - [x] Integration smoke tests across chat/summarization templates. - [x] Docs (console + examples) updated. - [x] Benchmarks run and summarized in this PR.

Benchmarks: (representative across test harness workloads, averages over 10 runs)
- Chat microbursts (median seq=64): cost/unit -9.3%, p50 latency +1.2%, p95 latency +2.9% (within SLO), safety-net triggered <1% of batches. 
- Single-turn long sequences (median seq=1024): cost/unit -14.8%, p50 latency +2.4%, p95 latency +3.1%, safety-net triggered 4.6% (fallback to fp16 variant; user-visible quality delta within tolerance). 
- Search/rerank (short seq, high concurrency): cost/unit -8.1%, latency unchanged.
Notes: numbers depend on workload mix; defaults bias toward conservative templates for high-quality tiers and more aggressive ones for cost-optimized tiers.

How to test locally: 1) Checkout branch and run unit tests: pytest serving/runtime/tests -k template -q 2) Run smoke harness: scripts/bench/run_workload.sh examples/econ/workload-templates/example-chat.yaml 3) Preview recommended templates in console: ./scripts/dev-console --load-template examples/econ/workload-templates/example-chat.yaml

Files changed (high-level): - serving/runtime/router/batch_templates.py: selector, scoring function, and caching logic (~420 LoC). - serving/runtime/quant_safety/net.py: proxy evaluator, fallback policy engine (~300 LoC). - serving/runtime/config/defaults.yaml: new templates and policy defaults. - console/docs: end-to-end docs + step-by-step on authoring templates. - tests: unit/integration coverage added; harness scripts extended.

Review conversation (highlights): - Oliver Reed: "Can we add a tighter CI test to emulate a quality regression so safety-net path is exercised in CI?" — Asha: "Added an integration smoke that injects a degraded quantized model and asserts fallback; included in the last commit (d4f6b90)." - Maya Gomez: "Please ensure telemetry doesn't leak PII in template fingerprints." — Asha: "Fingerprint uses aggregated metrics only (seq histogram, rate buckets), updated docs to call this out." - Sanjay Rao: "We should gate aggressive templates behind a rollout flag for Dedicated customers." — Asha: "Added a rollout flag and a console toggle; defaults remain conservative for Dedicated until enabled."

CI summary: initial pipeline failed lint on docs formatting; fixed in commit e5a0c11 and retriggered. All unit and integration suites passed on the final run. Benchmarks were executed on perf-canary infra and uploaded to S3 (link available in Linear ticket ENG-2249).

Risk and mitigation: The safety-net introduces a small additional CPU spike for sampled proxy evals; default sampling rate is 0.5% and can be tuned per-deployment. Fallbacks are recorded and surfaced in the console; we added an alert for safety-net firing above 1% over a 10m window.

Follow-ups planned: - Auto-tune templates from 7-day workload traces (ENG-2310) - Console UX for template trialing and canary rollout - Extend safety-net proxies to include small human-labeled prompt sets for selected customers
